official_sources.title: Practice guide 40 supplement 4: boundary agreements and determined boundaries
HM Land Registry plans: practice guides

verified_facts: General boundaries are sufficient for most titles but are not the same as determined boundaries.
A determined boundary is used where greater precision is required.
A determined boundary shows the exact line of the boundary for registration purposes.
HM Land Registry does not itself resolve a dispute about where the exact line lies.
The exact line must first be identified before HMLR records the boundary as determined.
A determined-boundary application must identify the exact line claimed.
The registrar must be able to identify adjoining owners for notice purposes.
A determined-boundary plan must show start, end and turning points.
A determined-boundary plan should include a statement describing the exact line.
The plan must show enough surrounding detail to identify its general position on the OS map.
The plan must state a scale; HMLR says the preferred scale is no smaller than 1:200.
HMLR INSPIRE GML is captured against the British National Grid.
British National Grid is EPSG:27700 in HMLR technical guidance.
Reprojection to web-map CRSs can introduce positional shift.
HMLR warns that some BNG-to-WGS84 reprojections may shift features by up to 15 metres.
quality_effect: Prevents treating indicative/general INSPIRE geometry as an exact legal boundary and blocks false sub-metre precision after reprojection.
